security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around MCP tool names, parameters, and examples. The skill has a real low-severity external MCP dependency and a medium operational risk because it can trigger authenticated Render deployments.

remediation.suggestion: Document that users connect to rube.app and should review Rube MCP trust, data handling, and account permissions before use.
Require explicit user confirmation before triggering deployments, clearing cache, or polling a production service.
Recommend least-privilege Render connections and warn users to verify the target service before each deployment.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Render connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `render`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `RENDER_LIST_SERVICES` - List all services with optional filters [Required]
- Pagination uses cursor-based approach; follow `cursor` until absent
- `clearCache`: Set `true` to clear build cache before deploying
- `serviceId` is required; resolve via LIST_SERVICES first
- `clearCache: true` forces a clean build; takes longer but resolves cache-related issues
- Use `cursor` from response for next page
- Continue until `cursor` is absent or results are empty
- Set `limit` to max (100) for fewer pagination rounds
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Poll at reasonable intervals (10-30 seconds) to avoid rate limits
- Avoid rapid polling; use 10-30 second intervals

content.user_title: Automate Render Deployments with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Render operations often require switching between service lists, deploy records, and project views. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for Render automation through Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Searches current Rube MCP tool schemas before using Render actions.
Lists Render services with name, type, limit, and cursor filters.
Triggers manual Render deployments for resolved service IDs.
Retrieves deployment status and interprets terminal deployment states.
Lists Render projects with cursor-based pagination.
Documents service ID, deploy ID, and pagination handling patterns.
limitations: Requires a connected Rube MCP server and an active Render connection.
Depends on the Render tools exposed by Rube MCP at runtime.
Does not create, modify, or delete Render services in the documented workflows.
Deployment polling must respect Render API rate limits.

use_cases.title: Service Inventory Review
use_cases.description: List Render services, filter by name or type, and collect service IDs for later operations.

use_cases.title: Manual Redeploy Workflow
use_cases.description: Find a service, trigger a deployment, and monitor progress until it succeeds or fails.

use_cases.title: Project Organization Check
use_cases.description: Browse Render projects and confirm which services are grouped for an environment or team.

prompt_templates.title: List My Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Render automation skill to list my Render services. Search the Rube MCP tools first, then show service names, types, and IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Service by Name
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Render services for the name "api". Resolve the exact service ID and tell me which matches are safe candidates for deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy and Monitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Render service named "production-api", ask for confirmation, trigger a deployment, and monitor it until it reaches a terminal state.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Deployment State
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest deployment for a Render service ID I provide. Retrieve the deployment status, explain failure states, and suggest next checks without changing the service.

output_examples.input: List all Render web services that include "api" in the name.
output_examples.output: The assistant searches the current Rube schemas, lists matching web services, and returns names, service IDs, and pagination notes.

output_examples.input: Redeploy the staging worker and watch the result.
output_examples.output: The assistant resolves the worker service ID, asks for confirmation, triggers the deployment, and reports status changes until completion.

output_examples.input: Show my Render projects and explain which one owns billing services.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists projects through the Render toolkit and summarizes project names, identifiers, and any relevant service grouping context.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP tools before each workflow so parameters match the current schema.
Resolve service names to service IDs before triggering deployment actions.
Use 10 to 30 second polling intervals when checking deployment status.
anti_patterns: Triggering deployments without confirming the target service and environment.
Polling deployment status rapidly enough to risk Render rate limits.
Assuming a service name is unique without checking the returned matches.

faq.question: Does this skill require Render API keys?
faq.answer: It uses Rube MCP with a connected Render account. Users still need an active Render connection in Rube.

faq.question: Can it deploy a Render service?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents how to resolve a service ID, trigger a deployment, and monitor the deployment status.

faq.question: Can it create new Render services?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows cover listing services, triggering deployments, retrieving deployments, and listing projects.

faq.question: Why does it search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change. Searching first helps the assistant use current parameters and tool names.

faq.question: Is this safe for production services?
faq.answer: It can affect production if connected to production Render services. Confirm the target service before deployment actions.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when Rube MCP is available.
